text:
The person wants the phone to read the screen out loud.
Read this to me.
Can you say what's on the screen?
My eyes are tired, so read the page aloud.
Out loud, please.
It's foggy outside and the words are hard to see today, so could you read them to me?
Start reading my messages and raise the volume a bit.
Read me my Monday emails. Actually, not all of them, only the ones from my sister.
I can't look at the screen right now, would you mind reading it for me?

Priya got home from her night shift at the hospital, tired and hungry. She still wore her work belt with the little scissors on it. She wanted to cook the soup her mother makes on a daily basis, but the recipe was for eight people and she was only cooking for four. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'This soup is for eight, but I only need half. Can you cut it down?' The speaker understood that she wanted the recipe scaled to half. It read out the new amounts: three cups of broth instead of six, one onion instead of two, and one spoon of salt instead of two. Then it reminded her to stir the pot every few minutes. Priya smiled, thanked it, and began chopping, glad she did not have to do the maths with such a sleepy head.

The person wants ideas for a birthday present for a friend.
Gift ideas for my friend?
What should I get Sam for his birthday?
I need a present that costs less than twenty dollars.
Got any ideas? Something small, not too fancy.
It's a cold month and her birthday is soon, so something warm would be nice, maybe a scarf.
I have only a few days left and no clue what to buy, can you help?
Suggest something more unusual than a candle or a mug.
Would you please give me three gift ideas for my dad, who loves coffee, maybe something for his drip machine?

Person: My sink is leaking. Can you get someone to fix it?
Assistant: I'm sorry about the leak. Which day would you like the repair person to come?
Person: Tomorrow, please. Wait, no, my dad is at work tomorrow. Make it Saturday.
Assistant: Okay, Saturday. Is it the kitchen sink or the bathroom sink?
Person: The kitchen one. Mom was washing a raw onion and the water started dripping under it.
Assistant: Thank you. What time on Saturday?
Person: In the morning. I love mornings.
Assistant: Great. I'll ask for a repair visit on Saturday morning for the kitchen sink. Is that right?
Person: Yes. Thank you!

Tom rode his bicycle to the office and sat down at his desk. His tooth had been aching for a whole week, and he kept pressing his cheek. He took out his phone and said, 'My tooth is killing me, but I can't miss work again.' The phone understood that he needed a dentist and that he wanted a time outside of his busy hours. It looked at the dentists near the office and found one that opens at eight in the morning. It said there was a free spot on Thursday at eight fifteen. Tom said that sounded good, so the phone booked the visit, added it to his calendar, and set a reminder for the night before. Tom felt better already and went back to his emails.

The person wants to book a haircut.
Book me a haircut.
I need a trim, can I get a slot on Friday?
Is there a free spot at the barber this week?
Find a salon that isn't too far from home and book a cut for Saturday.
Please fill in a time for my haircut and tell me the shop's opening hours.
Can you check if the barber has an hour block free tomorrow afternoon?
My hair is a mess, get me in somewhere soon.
Would you be so kind as to make an appointment with my usual hairdresser and send me a reminder the day before?

Email is a way to send a message to someone far away and get an answer back when they have time. Your inbox is where new messages arrive. Most people change a few things about it. They mark mail as read or unread, move old mail into folders, and attach photos or files to a new message. When you ask an assistant for help, you can say, 'Write an email to my boss,' or 'Show me the unread mail,' or 'Attach that photo and send it.' It is smart to be careful with the name in the address box, so the right person gets it. You can also say, 'Delete the old ones' or 'Read my newest message to me.'

Omar had just moved to a new city, and most of his things were still in boxes in the closet. He found his running shoes and wanted to try the park nearby. He said to his phone, 'Find me a running route of five kilometres, and keep it flat.' The phone understood that he wanted a flat loop of about five kilometres starting from his flat, and it showed him a path around the lake. Then Omar remembered his meeting. 'No, wait, make it three kilometres. I can't skip breakfast and I'm late.' The phone changed the route to a shorter loop of three kilometres and said the maximum hill on it was very small. It also said the run would take about twenty minutes. Omar tied his laces and went out.

The person wants the pet feeder to give the dog his dinner.
Feed the dog.
Give Max his dinner, please.
Time for the dog's food.
Put out a scoop of dry food for Max.
Wait, he's had a long day, so make it two scoops instead.
He's staring at his bowl, so I think he wants his dinner.
Fill the bowl, but no corn, it upsets his tummy.
Could you please start the feeder? I'm stuck in traffic and he's been alone since morning.

Luis parked his delivery truck at a rest stop and took a break. He opened his phone and said, 'Show me what my sister posted today, but do not show me any ads.' The phone understood that he wanted to read only his sister's new posts and not the ads in between. It opened her page and read out the latest one: a photo of a woman at her bakery, holding a sweet cake with lemon on top. Luis laughed. 'Like it, and tell her I'll join the family dinner on Sunday.' The phone pressed the like button and sent a short reply saying Luis would join the dinner. Then it asked if he wanted to hear the next post. 'No, that's enough,' said Luis, and he started the truck.

Dana was packing lunches when the wifi stopped being fun. The kids' tablets were still on, and she needed them put away for just one more minute. She picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'turn of the internet on the kids tablets for an hour'. She had spelled 'off' wrong, but the assistant understood anyway. It figured she wanted the internet paused on the two tablets for sixty minutes, and nothing else. The router light flashed once, and the tablets showed a small message that the internet was paused. The assistant told her it would come back on at nine o'clock. Dana said that was fine, and went back to cutting the sandwiches.

An appointment is a time you keep for someone, like a haircut, a dentist, or a doctor. It is for making sure the person is ready for you, so you do not wait in a long line. People often change appointments. They move them to another day, or they skip one when they are sick and cancel it. When they ask an assistant, they might say, 'Book me a haircut on Friday,' or 'Push my dentist to next week,' or 'What time does the shop open?' A loud alarm or a reminder message the day before helps people remember. A skirt that needs fixing, for example, can be taken to the tailor at a booked time.

A car needs a little care to run well. Fuel is what makes it go, and tyre pressure is how much air is in the wheels. For some people, looking after a car is a hobby, but for most it is just a chore. People often change small things: they fill up the tank, add air to the tyres, or warm up the car on a cold morning. If the car makes a strange noise, you should have it checked. When asking an assistant, people say things like 'How much fuel is left?', 'Are my tyres okay?', 'Start the car, it's freezing,' or 'Where did I park?' You can also scroll through the car screen to see the numbers yourself.

name: show_subtitles
does: Puts written words on the screen so you can read what the people in a show are saying.
inputs: the show or channel, and whether the words should be on or off
people say:
- I can't hear what they're saying
- The actors mumble, put the words on the screen
- My hearing is weak tonight, help me follow this
- Show me the words until the movie finishes
- It's a long stretch of fast talking and I keep missing it

Person: Hello, I hope you can help me. I am buying an iron fence for the north side of my garden, and I need to know the price after the discount, so I can tell my wife before we go to the shop.
Assistant: Happy to help. What is the full price, and how much is the discount?
Person: The fence costs 240 dollars, and the discount is 15 percent.
Assistant: Fifteen percent of 240 is 36, so the fence will cost 204 dollars.
Person: Wonderful. And what would four of them cost?
Assistant: Four times 204 is 816 dollars.
Person: Thank you, that is very kind of you.

Maya worked in an office and had to plan lunch for her team. She said to her phone, 'Find a place for six people near work, but not the Italian place, we went there last week.' The phone understood she wanted a lunch table for six, and not at that restaurant. It read out a few options and sorted them by how close they were. The closest was a noodle shop. Maya added, 'One of us is bringing a child, so I need a high chair.' The phone asked the shop for a table at the exact time Maya wanted, twelve thirty. The shop had a table with a high chair free. The phone booked it and told Maya the address.

Ben was nine years old, and he had just fixed the wheel on his bike. He wanted to get stronger so he could ride faster. He asked the speaker in the living room, 'Can you wake me up tomorrow at seven and show me an exercise?' The speaker understood that he wanted an alarm for seven in the morning and a simple workout. It set the alarm and said, 'Tomorrow at seven, I'll tell you how to do ten jumping jacks and five push-ups.' Ben said that sounded fun. Then he asked if the park gym was open, and the speaker said it was closed until the weekend, so they could use the backyard instead. Ben smiled and went to bed.

A cup of coffee or tea is a small break in the day. The drink is made to taste the way you like, so people change how strong it is, how sweet, and how big. Some like a weak tea with no sugar, and others want a strong coffee with two spoons of sugar. When an assistant helps, you can say, 'Make it stronger,' 'Less sweet, please,' or 'Fill it up.' If your cup is empty, you can ask for another. On pizza night, many families make a big jug of lemonade, and children look forward to it all week. You can even ask for it by saying, 'Make the lemonade a little sweeter.'

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who liked to read in the evening, but the light in her living room was too bright. She said to the speaker, 'Excuse me, my eyes get tired when I read, and the ceiling light is very bright. Would you please make it softer, and a little warmer, so I can finish my book?' The assistant understood that she wanted the living room light dimmer and in a warmer colour. It lowered the brightness to about thirty percent and chose a warm yellow. She sat down with her black cat and a cup of tea, with a fork and a slice of cake on the table. The bulb gave off no heat, but the colour made the room feel warm.

name: read_screen_aloud
does: Speaks the words on the screen out loud, so a person who cannot see them well can listen instead.
inputs: which text to read, and how fast to speak
people say:
- Tell me what it says
- I can't see this small writing, say it for me
- My eyes are too tired to read, I would choose to listen
- Is it true that the email is from my bank? Read me what it says
- The soup recipe is too small to read, read it to me
- Say the page slowly

Grandpa Joe was not good with technology. He stood in the laundry room holding yesterday's newspaper and a pile of dirty towels. He had tried for years to fix the old washer himself, but it was too hard. 'Start the washing machine with a double rinse and tell me when it's done,' he said to the little speaker. The speaker understood two things: he wanted the towel cycle with an extra rinse, and he wanted to be told at the end. It started the machine and said it would take fifty minutes. Joe sat down with his newspaper. When the machine finished, the speaker said, 'Your towels are done.' 'Well I never,' said Joe.

Sometimes people have to do things away from home, like go to the post office or the bank. These errands are for sending a letter, paying a bill, or picking up a parcel. People change when they go, because shops have opening hours and the line may be long. If you need to ship a package before a deadline, you must get there before closing. When asking an assistant for help, people say, 'When does the post office close?', 'Remind me to go to the bank at noon,' 'How far away is the closest branch?', or 'Move my errands to Saturday.'

A meeting at work is a time when people talk about the same thing. Before it starts, someone writes an agenda, which is a short list of what to talk about. People join by a link on a call, and then they share their screen so everyone can see the same slides. Some people take notes with a pen, while others type. A day full of meetings can be tiring, so people ask to move or shorten them. They say, 'Join my ten o'clock call,' 'Share my screen,' 'Push this meeting back an hour,' or 'Sweep my afternoon clear.'

Rosa owned a small shop. Her workers had spent all week building a new window display, and she wanted to thank them with dinner. While she listened to an audiobook in the back room, she paused it and said to her phone, 'Book a table for twenty-five on Friday at seven, somewhere with a big room.' The phone understood that she wanted a restaurant with a large space for twenty-five people. It found one with a long room that it only used for temporary parties. The restaurant said yes, and the phone booked the table and sent Rosa the address. Rosa started her audiobook again, happy that dinner was done.

name: sort_my_waste
does: Says which bin an item belongs in, such as recycling, compost or general waste.
inputs: the item, in plain words
people say:
- Can I put a coffee filter in the compost?
- Where does this pizza box go?
- Is this plastic or paper?
- Is it a great idea to put glass in the blue bin?
- Please repeat which bin takes cans

name: read_recipe_steps
does: Reads the steps of a dish one at a time, in the right order, from a saved recipe.
inputs: the name of the dish, and which step to start from
people say:
- What's the next step?
- Read me my grandmother's pancake recipe from my personal collection
- Where was I in the cake? Go back one step
- Walk me through the soup in order
- Give me the steps, I don't want to look at the book with my sticky hands

name: find_next_train
does: Looks up when the next trains leave a station and says which ones are late or have a toilet on board.
inputs: the station, and the time you want to leave
people say:
- Is there a train to the city soon?
- When is the final train tonight?
- Which train has a toilet on it?
- The man who used to sell tickets has gone home, when's the next one to Leeds?
- Will my train be late?

Lena was a student waiting at a bus stop on a sunny afternoon. Her phone buzzed, and she saw the bus was late. She did not feel like typing, so she just said, 'Next bus?' The phone understood that she meant the next bus at her stop, and it said bus 12 would come in seven minutes. Lena wanted to pick up her pills at the pharmacy before class. She said, 'Track it,' and the phone began to follow the bus on the map. When the bus was two minutes away, it buzzed again. Lena looked up and saw the bus turn the corner.

The person wants the robot mower to cut the lawn.
Mow the lawn.
Start the mower.
Get the grass cut this afternoon.
The grass looks too long, can you send the robot out?
I invited friends over on Saturday, so please cut the lawn before then.
Mow the back yard. No wait, the front yard first.
Speaking into the microphone on the garden app: cut the grass, please.
Could you please have the robot mow the grass? I want it nice and comfortable for the kids to play on.

Person: how much is 45 split between 5 friends
Assistant: Each friend pays 9.
Person: ok now add the parking money but dont include the drinks
Assistant: How much was the parking?
Person: 12
Assistant: Parking split five ways is 2.40 each, so each friend pays 11.40 in total, with no drinks.
Person: good. we got pink lemonade and i didnt even drink any lol
Assistant: Then it is right to leave it out. Each friend pays 11.40.

Time management means using your day so the important things get done. A focus timer is a simple tool: you work for twenty-five minutes, then you take a short break. Routines help too, like a morning list so the day does not feel messy. People who stick to a plan often feel they win back their evenings. They change the timer or the break, and ask an assistant, 'Start a focus timer,' 'Make my breaks longer,' or 'Remind me to stretch at three.' Someone making breakfast with butter and toast can even set a ten-minute timer to get out the door on time.

name: change_alarm_time
does: Moves the morning alarm to a new time so you wake up well rested.
inputs: the new time, and which days it should ring
people say:
- Swap my alarm to six thirty
- I want to sleep in tomorrow
- Wake me half an hour later
- I need to be up earlier for the train
- I'm going to the plant sale early, make it five
- Don't ring on Sunday

Grandma Ruth wanted to have lunch with her friend Carol. She picked up her phone and said, 'Put lunch with Carol on Wednesday at noon.' The phone understood she wanted a new event on her calendar and added it. Then Ruth remembered that Carol's plane doesn't land until Wednesday night. 'Oh, no, I mean Thursday.' She asked the phone to compare her free times on Wednesday and Thursday, and it said she was free at noon on Thursday. The phone moved the event to Thursday at noon. Ruth added, 'Put a note on it: no raw fish for lunch, Carol doesn't like it.' The phone saved the note and gave her a thumbs up.

The person wants the bedroom blinds closed.
Close the blinds.
Shut the curtains.
Blinds down, please.
It's too bright in here, I can't see the TV.
The sun is in my eyes.
The sun is fading all my toys, shut it out.
Close the blinds I labelled bedroom, and do it straight away.
It's so bright in this room that I can't take a nap, would you mind doing something about it?

Person: Brr, it's freezing in here.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which room are you in?
Person: The bedroom. I just moved in and my suitcase is still on the floor.
Assistant: Okay. How warm would you like the bedroom to be?
Person: I don't know. Not too hot.
Assistant: How about twenty-one degrees?
Person: Yes, good. My dinner was cooked an hour ago and it's already cold, and the window is wet. I'll wipe it later.
Assistant: Sounds good. I have set the bedroom heating to twenty-one degrees.

Mr. Evans had a new smart speaker, but he was not good with technology. He sat in his armchair, tired after a long day at his job. He looked at the speaker and said, 'It's a bit quiet in here, I can't hear the fancy music my daughter sent me.' The speaker understood that he wanted the music louder. It raised the volume a little and asked, 'Is that better?' Mr. Evans did not know how to drag a slider on the phone, but he did not have to. He just said, 'Still too quiet,' and the speaker made it louder again. This time he smiled and closed his eyes.

Chen had just moved to a new city and did not know a single restaurant. His neighbour had told him about a place with good dumplings. He said to his phone, 'Excuse me, I would like to find a small restaurant that makes dumplings, because my mother is visiting this weekend and I want to treat her to something nice. Could you please book us a table for two on Saturday evening?' The phone understood that he wanted a dumpling restaurant and a table for two. It found a place near his flat that makes fresh dumplings daily and booked seven o'clock. Chen thanked it. He still had to mop the floors and shave before she arrived.

name: group_speakers
does: Joins several speakers in different rooms so they all play the same music at once.
inputs: which rooms to join, and what to play
people say:
- Play the same song everywhere for my Tuesday party
- Let the music leak into the hall
- I want the north bedroom to sound like the kitchen
- Put all the speakers on the same song
- Take the garden speaker out of the group

The person wants to know the score of tonight's match.
What's the score?
Who's winning?
Did the Reds win?
Tell me how my team is doing, it's been twenty minutes since I checked.
Is the match over yet, or are they still playing?
Dinner is cooked and I'm not watching, so what's the score?
I'm going to chill on the couch, so just tell me when someone scores.
Did the Reds win by more than twenty-five points? Wait, I mean the Blues.

name: send_text
does: Writes a text message to a person you name and sends it.
inputs: who it is for, and what it should say
people say:
- Tell Dad I'll be late
- Message Sam that the washer is fixed
- Text my sister to say get well, I hope she heals fast
- Let Anna know to double-check the time
- Send Mom a quick hello

Lights help us see, read and feel comfortable at home. A lamp is easy to move, but a ceiling light lights the whole room. Smart bulbs let you change the brightness and the colour without getting up. In the evening, people like a warm, soft light, but to read or cook they want it clear and bright. A museum puts a spotlight on a painting so it is clear to see, and at home you can do the same thing with a lamp. People say, 'Make it brighter,' 'Dim the lights,' 'Turn off the lamp,' or 'Change the bulb to blue.'

Sam the cook was making dinner when the cat began to meow at his feet. The cat's seat by the window was empty, and her bowl was empty too. Sam's hands were covered in flour, so he just said, 'Feed Whiskers.' The speaker understood that he meant to give the cat her food now, and it told the automatic feeder to put out a scoop. The cat ate happily. 'Strange,' Sam thought, 'she's usually not hungry until six.' He also asked the speaker to text his wife that the cat was eating early. The speaker sent the message and Sam went back to his dough.

Food delivery brings a meal to your door. You pick the food on a phone, say where you are, and a driver brings it, sometimes across a river or through the rain. People change the address, the time, or the tip. A polite tip is a few dollars, and many people add more when the weather is bad. When asking an assistant for help, people say, 'Order me a burger,' 'Make the tip three dollars,' 'Send it to my office instead,' or 'How long until it comes?' The assistant can also tell you when the driver is close.

Person: Can you heat the pool for the kids?
Assistant: Sure. What temperature would you like?
Person: Thirty degrees. Wait, that's too hot. Make it twenty-eight.
Assistant: Twenty-eight degrees, got it. When should it be ready?
Person: By four o'clock. It might rain this afternoon, though.
Assistant: Should I close the cover if it starts to rain?
Person: Yes, please. And keep the water clear. Did you add the salt?
Assistant: I can't check the salt, I'm sorry. I can only set the heat and the cover.

Mr. Park owned a small shop and was about to leave for the evening. He wanted to make it safer. He said to his phone, 'Show me the back door camera, and I have an idea: make the motion alarm more sensitive tonight, double what it is now.' The phone understood that he wanted to see the camera on the display and raise the alarm setting to twice the level. It showed the back door, where nothing was moving, and doubled the motion setting. Then it said the alarm would arm itself soon after he locked the front door, in about ten minutes. Mr. Park nodded, picked up his coat and turned off the lights.

name: keep_score
does: Counts the points for each player in a game and says who is ahead.
inputs: the players' names, and the points to add up
people say:
- Keep the score for me while we play, we're eating salad
- It's half time, who is ahead?
- Count up our points
- Give Mia five more
- Who's winning the game?
- Start us all from zero again

A front door keeps your home safe, and a lock decides who can come in. Some locks use keys, and some use a code or a phone. A garage door opens to let in the car. People change a lot of things: they lock up at night, let a friend in, or check who is at the door. When asking an assistant, they say things like 'Lock the front door,' 'Did I shut the garage?', 'Who's out there?', or 'Open up for my sister.' A lamp by the door and a yellow light on the porch help people see who is there, and a locked door helps you win a good night's sleep.

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use. It is written for a set number of servings, like four people. When more or fewer people will eat, you scale it up or down. If a man is cooking for eight, he doubles everything. Cups and spoons are the usual tools, and a loose measure like a pinch is fine for salt, but measure flour carefully. People say, 'Make this for two,' 'Double the recipe,' or 'How many tablespoons are in a cup?' You can also ask the assistant to draw up a shopping list for the dish.

Arithmetic is the plain maths we use every day: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing. We use it when we pay a bill, split a cost, or double a recipe. People use words like 'plus', 'minus', 'times' and 'divided by'. They also say, 'What is 20 plus 10?', 'Take 5 from 30,' 'Share 12 among 3 people,' or 'How much are 4 of these at 6 dollars each?' A computer does it fast, but it is smart to be careful with the numbers you give it. You can let a hot drink cool while you work out the tip.

Person: I need a room for next weekend.
Assistant: Happy to help. Which city?
Person: Lisbon. I don't want a hostel, I want a real hotel.
Assistant: Got it. How many nights, and how many guests?
Person: Two nights, just me. I read the news that it will freeze at night, so I want heating.
Assistant: Which dates?
Person: Friday and Saturday.
Assistant: Okay. I'll look for hotels in Lisbon with heating and recent good reviews, for one guest, Friday and Saturday.
